items.stem: A team wants the agent to never read files in a secrets folder, in every clone. A note in CLAUDE.md asks the agent to avoid that folder. The block must hold even when the model ignores the note. Which change meets the constraint?
options: Deploy the deny rule in managed settings, and add a sandbox on every developer machine.
Add the deny rule to the personal local settings of the team lead only.
Add a Read deny rule for the secrets folder in the committed settings file.
Add a PostToolUse hook that blocks reads of the secrets folder.
items.rationale: A deny rule in the committed settings file reaches every clone after a pull. The rule blocks the read before the tool runs, so the result does not depend on the model.
items.trap: A PostToolUse hook that blocks reads looks like enforcement, but that hook runs only after the tool call succeeds.

items.stem: A team wants a research subagent that only reads files. The subagent must not receive any write tool. Which setup meets the constraint?
options: Set the tools field to Read and Grep, and add a second reviewer subagent for each folder.
Create the subagent without a tools field, and add a CLAUDE.md line that forbids edits.
Set the model field to read-only, which blocks write tools for the subagent.
Set the subagent tools field to Read and Grep only.
items.rationale: The tools field limits the tools that a subagent can use. Read and Grep cannot write files, so the role stays read-only.
items.trap: A CLAUDE.md line that forbids edits looks like a restriction, but a subagent without a tools field inherits every tool.

items.stem: A team needs one enforced rule on every clone. One developer also needs a personal exception that does not weaken the team rule. Select two actions that meet both needs.
options: Commit the team deny rule in the shared settings file.
Put the team deny rule in the user settings file of each developer.
Put a personal allow rule for one extra command in the local settings file, which stays out of git.
Put the team deny rule in CLAUDE.md, which Claude Code enforces as a permission.
items.rationale: The shared settings file applies to every clone after a pull. The local file stays out of git, and a deny rule from any scope still applies.
items.trap: A personal settings file looks flexible, but it cannot enforce the rule across the team.
